Theme

Nature & food

muddy adjective

also miry, slimy, covered in mud

classical

Hirt. B. Alex. 5: aqua (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 2.135: lacus (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Am. 3.6.1: rīpae (Lewis & Short)

līmōsus, līmōsa, līmōsum

declension

full of mud or slime, miry

From līmus, slime, mud.

Other words

  • lutulentus, lutulenta, lutulentum — muddy, covered in mud

    declension · classical · Hor. Ep. 2.2.75: sūs (Lewis & Short); Ov. Met. 1.434: tellūs (Lewis & Short); Ov. Am. 3.6.95: amnis (Lewis & Short)

    From lutum, mud.

Examples

  • līmōsōque novae saliunt in gurgite rānae

    and as new-made frogs they leap in the muddy poolOv. Met. 6.381

See also mud, marshy, puddle, wallow, dirty, swamp.

SourcesLewis & Short: limosus · Lewis & Short: lutulentus

Ovid, Metamorphoses 6.381.
